question: Should OpenClaw support sandboxed requesters spawning ACP sessions by running harnesses in a sandbox, by adding a host-side bridge/proxy, or by folding the behavior into the broader execution-backend placement contract?
rationale: The next step defines a sandbox/host trust boundary plus public config and model-facing tool semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent security design.

options.title: Design sandbox-aware ACP boundary
options.body: Define a narrow bridge or placement contract for ACP spawn/steer/cancel with explicit auth, audit, workspace, secret, rate-limit, and cleanup rules before implementation.

options.title: Require harnesses inside sandbox
options.body: Keep the current host-side ACP block and document running the harness inside the sandbox container as the supported path for this workflow.

options.title: Defer to execution backends
options.body: Keep this issue open as an acceptance case while the broader execution-backend placement design settles remote-worker security semantics.

recommendation.title: Design sandbox-aware ACP boundary
recommendation.body: Define a narrow bridge or placement contract for ACP spawn/steer/cancel with explicit auth, audit, workspace, secret, rate-limit, and cleanup rules before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest direct history on sessions_spawn and ACP sandbox policy, including the original tool, limitation docs, and slash-command block.
